description: HAL PWM input: TIM3 CH1 PA6 generates 2 kHz/30 %, 5 kHz/50 %, 1.25 kHz/75 % (1 s each); TIM2 CH1 PA0 measures it (jumper PA6 -> PA0), prints 'f=<Hz> d=<permille>'
expect: 72 MHz; USART1 PA9 115200 8N1. Bench: a jumper from PA6 to PA0. First TX: 'PWM input: TIM3 CH1 PA6 -> TIM2 CH1 PA0\r\n'. TIM3 CH1 (PA6, PWM mode 1, PSC 0) outputs 2000 Hz 30 % (ARR 35999, CCR1 10800) for the first second after start, then 5000 Hz 50 % (14399 / 7200), then 1250 Hz 75 % (57599 / 43200), repeating every 3 s; ARR and CCR1 are preloaded so each change applies at an update event. TIM2 (PSC 0) in PWM input mode: IC1 = TI1FP1 rising -> CCR1, IC2 = TI1FP2 falling -> CCR2, slave reset on TI1FP1; period = CCR1 + 1 and high time = CCR2 + 1 counts (the capture latches the counter before the reset, RM0008 Figure 113); URS = 1, so only a real overflow (no rising edge for 65536 counts) raises the update interrupt, which clears the measurement. Every 250 ms (first 125 ms after start, never at a switch) it prints 'f=<72 MHz / period> d=<1000 x high / period>' rounded: 'f=2000 d=300' (4 lines), 'f=5000 d=500' (4 lines), 'f=1250 d=750' (4 lines), repeating. Without the jumper PA0 sees no edge and every line is 'f=0 d=0'.

circuit: USART1: virtual terminal on PA9 (TX) / PA10 (RX)

boot.USART1: PWM input: TIM3 CH1 PA6 -> TIM2 CH1 PA0
